📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #31 (cumulative total; degraded-mode DD-scan-diff cycle, no Slack MCP this session).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience`
Playbook: monitor 302056327 fires but the metric never approaches the 1s threshold when re-queried — monitor/data artifact, not real latency. Confirm via re-query at a wider rollup + 0 error logs. [full playbook in kb/known-issues.json]
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total):
  • none — no Slack MCP this session (DD-scan-diff synthetic alert, monitor 302056327, fired 2026-08-08T08:43:07Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
  • DD metric (10s interval, re-query of the monitor's own eval window ± wider range): single outlier point at 08:30:00Z = 44260.98s (clearly a rollup artifact, not real). Re-queried the SAME window at a 60s rollup (`.rollup(avg,60)`): max value drops to 0.133s, min 0.001s — the outlier vanishes entirely. https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request.p95&exp_scope=service%3Anotifications%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1786177087&end=1786179487
  • DD logs `service:notifications status:error env:prod` for the monitor's exact 10-min eval window (08:33:07–08:43:07Z): 0 hits — confirms playbook step 2 (not previously separately confirmed on either prior occurrence; now confirmed on this, the 3rd). https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Anotifications%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1786177987000&to_ts=1786178587000&live=false
  • NOTE for Ben: this KB entry's `match.channels` lists `["alert-system","swat"]`, but the DD monitor's own Slack routing tag is `@slack-alert-runtime-monitoring` (confirmed from the monitor's raw `message` field) — the channel list looks stale/never-verified against the monitor config. Matched this cycle by direct monitor-ID+name text match despite the channel-scope mismatch; recommend updating `match.channels` to include `alert-runtime-monitoring`.
  • Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-08-08-b5f97d36f8f523c0.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #113 (cumulative total; degraded-mode DD-scan-diff cycle, no Slack MCP this session).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience (runtime-core-subscriber-api) / Admin (mobile-notifications-stack)` — split per ownership.md, DD tag says team:crm for both
Playbook: sibling AMQP-consumer heartbeat/throughput monitors trip on genuine but benign quiet-period traffic dips, then self-recover within minutes, 0 corroborating errors. Confirm via metric dip + 0 error logs on the fired service. [full playbook in kb/known-issues.json]
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total):
  • none — no Slack MCP this session (DD-scan-diff synthetic alert, monitor 302055141 "[CRM] method-mobile-notifications-subscriber heartbeat — consumer silent", fired 2026-08-08T10:04:21Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302055141
  • DD metric `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()`: no points below the 0.005 msg/s alert floor found in the ±20min window around the eval window — this service's raw metric is extremely sparse (documented in the KB as ~35 datapoints across a 3h+ window; quiet minutes are normal), consistent with the KB's benign-quiet-period shape. Now recovered (overall_state: OK). https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1786181661&end=1786184061
  • DD logs `service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber status:error env:prod` for the 60-min eval window (09:04:21–10:04:21Z): 0 hits. https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1786179861000&to_ts=1786183461000&live=false
  • Sibling monitor 302057011 (runtime-core-subscriber throughput) also fired this same cycle 10 min later under the same KB entry — see docs/investigations/2026-08-08-65c27469a4cb442c.md, suppressed as same-cycle KIR-gate-ordering (this post's own send bumps `last_notified_at` to now, so the later sibling lands inside the 24h window seconds after).
  • Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-08-08-4bd761745a371bd7.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #46 (cumulative total; degraded-mode DD-scan-diff cycle, no Slack MCP this session).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations`
Playbook: monitor 296641466 goes No Data on a genuinely quiet integration-event period; always check sibling P1 monitors (296632224 Event ingest stopped, 296636101 Kafka events stopped) first — if both OK, core EDA pipeline is healthy and this is very unlikely to be user-impacting. [full playbook in kb/known-issues.json]
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total):
  • none — no Slack MCP this session (DD-scan-diff synthetic alert, monitor 296641466 "[EDA][Consumer][P3] Integration events (AMQP) stopped publishing", fired 2026-08-08T10:23:26Z, No Data)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296641466
  • Sibling P1 monitors checked per playbook step 2: 296632224 (Event ingest stopped) `overall_state: OK`, last modified 2026-07-23; 296636101 (Kafka events stopped) `overall_state: OK`, last modified 2026-07-23 — both stable/healthy, core EDA pipeline not affected.
  • DD logs `service:eda_consumer status:error env:prod` for the 30-min eval window (09:53:26–10:23:26Z): 0 hits. https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aeda_consumer%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1786179206000&to_ts=1786181006000&live=false
  • Re-checked live during this cycle: monitor has already self-recovered (`overall_state: OK`, new last_triggered_ts 2026-08-08T11:24:27Z), matching this KB entry's documented fast self-recovery shape.
  • Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-08-08-e0f8bcca8533532b.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #260 (cumulative total; degraded-mode DD-scan-diff cycle, no Slack MCP this session).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience`
Playbook: latency-only recurring p95 spikes on runtime-core-api RTC Screen Load / Action Execution, zero error logs, self-recovers. Confirm via `dd_search.py metric` on the resource + confirm 0 errors. [full playbook in kb/known-issues.json]
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total):
  • none — no Slack MCP this session (DD-scan-diff synthetic alert, monitor 115456700 "RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency", fired 2026-08-08T10:37:20Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700
  • DD metric `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}` over the eval window (10:22:20–10:37:20Z): 2 points over the 3s threshold — 6.47s @10:23:40Z, 9.09s @10:29:50Z (peak). https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20%40duration%3A%3E5s&start=1786184540000&end=1786185440000
  • Confirmed latency-only: `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` for the same window returned 0 hits. https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1786184540000&to_ts=1786185440000&live=false
  • No ki-21 (gateway-microservices-timeout) co-fire this cycle — its last occurrence was 00:46:11Z, ~10h earlier, outside the 60-min shared-upstream co-fire window per this KB's precedence_note.
  • Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-08-08-b0d51d1f8bdcae37.md
